answer: A verifiable delay function turns time itself into the Sybil tax. Each epoch, a public beacon broadcasts a random seed, and every agent must compute a sequential delay puzzle bound to its identity before it may act. The puzzle cannot be parallelised, so one machine can only advance one identity at a time. Its proof is stored in the agent's vault record, and a pearl token is issued only after the delay is verified. Spinning up a thousand fake agents would require a thousand machines running in lockstep, while honest agents pay only a few seconds each.
